chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the cameleer who breaks what he carries or spills it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is trustworthy, there is nothing upon him, but if he is not trustworthy, he is liable.'
ai.seo_question: What is the liability of a carrier if they break or spill the goods they are transporting?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the principle of *dhaman* (liability) in commercial contracts, distinguishing between a trustworthy carrier (*ma'mun*) who bears no liability for accidental damage and an untrustworthy one who is fully liable. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the carrier's moral and professional integrity as the primary determinant of risk allocation in pre-modern trade logistics. The ruling underscores the legal concept that trustworthiness (*amanah*) serves as a shield against liability, whereas its absence imposes strict responsibility for loss.
